Attackers with two ordinary accounts can download the attachment via GET /v1/attachment, where the negative price increases the buyer's wallet balance, minting funds to purchase other users' paid attachments.

t: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 Stored XSS via #topic Highlighting in Posts
d: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject script by abusing #topic link wrapping in preparePost and parsePostTag. Attackers can publish posts or comments with a crafted topic containing a lone '<' and event handler to steal the PAOPAO_TOKEN JWT from localStorage and take over viewer accounts.

t: Rocboss paopao-ce 0.2.0 through 0.6.0-alpha.3 Path Traversal in LocalOSS File Deletion
d: Rocboss paopao-ce 0.2.0 through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a path traversal vulnerability in LocalOSS DeleteObject that allows authenticated users to delete arbitrary files by submitting crafted media values. Attackers can send dot-dot-slash sequences in the avatar or media content to POST /v1/user/avatar or POST /v1/post/comment, deleting server-writable files including configuration and data.

t: SamWaf 1.0.128 through 1.3.25-beta.11 WAF Bypass via Chunked or Oversized Request Body
d: SamWaf 1.0.128 through 1.3.25-beta.11 contains a request body inspection bypass vulnerability in WafEngine.ServeHTTP that skips bodies with chunked encoding or lengths of 2048 bytes or more. Remote unauthenticated attackers can send SQL injection, XSS, command injection, traversal or upload payloads chunked or padded, which reach the protected backend uninspected.

t: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 Paid Attachment Payment Bypass via Post Detail
d: Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain paid attachments by reading storage URLs from the GET /v1/post endpoint. Attackers can download the paid file directly from the unauthenticated LocalOSS /oss static route, whose signed URL expired parameter is never checked.

t: REBUILD 2.7.0 through 4.5.4 SQL Injection via plan Parameter in /project/tasks/list
d: REBUILD 2.7.0 through 4.5.4 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject AjQL conditions through the plan parameter of /project/tasks/list. Attackers can use priority-* plans and the returned task count as a boolean oracle to recover a task creator's SHA-256 password hash and log in as that user, including the administrator.

t: REBUILD 3.5.0 through 4.5.4 Privilege Escalation via roleId Mass Assignment
d: REBUILD 3.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify their own roleId through mass assignment in /app/entity/record-save and /app/entity/common-save. Attackers can submit their own User record with roleId set to the built-in administrator role, bypassing updatable=false restrictions to gain full administrator privileges.

t: REBUILD 4.3.0 through 4.5.4 Privilege Escalation via /commons/file-preview CSRF Token Leak
d: REBUILD 4.3.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to obtain a SYSTEM_USER token by requesting /commons/file-preview with an arbitrary src value. Attackers can read the leaked _csrfToken from the redirect Location header and send it as X-AuthToken to access the admin center and administrative APIs.

t: REBUILD 4.5.0 through 4.5.4 Password Hash Disclosure via MCP QueryRecords
d: REBUILD 4.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to recover the administrator password hash by filtering User.password through the MCP QueryRecords tool. Attackers can send LK2 prefix-match filters to the /gw/mcp/sse gateway and use the returned total count as an oracle to extract the SHA-256 hash one character at a time, then log in as administrator.

t: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 Information Disclosure via /api/v1/config/defaults
d: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve server secrets through the /api/v1/config/defaults endpoint. Attackers can send a GET request to obtain the operator's LLM provider API keys and GitHub or GitLab tokens, then abuse those services and accessible repositories.

t: OfficeCLI 1.0.56 through 1.0.161 Stored XSS via Watch Preview List Marker Color
d: OfficeCLI 1.0.56 through 1.0.161 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the officecli watch preview that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped numbering w:color values. Attackers can craft a DOCX whose color closes the style element, then abuse the unauthenticated /api/batch endpoint to read local files and modify the watched document.

t: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 File Read and SSRF via PDF Report Subtitle
d: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in ReportGenerator.generate_task_report that allows registered users to read server files and perform SSRF. Attackers can create a project whose name contains a link attachment element and download the task PDF report to retrieve local files or internal network responses.

t: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 SSRF via Project Branch Listing Leaks Git Tokens
d: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

t: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 Path Traversal via upload-zip Project ID
d: DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write arbitrary files by importing projects with crafted IDs. Attackers can set absolute or ../ project IDs via /api/v1/database/import, then upload ZIPs through /api/v1/scan/upload-zip following cloned symlinks to overwrite app/main.py for remote code execution.

t: Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 Information Disclosure via Site-Wide Change History
d: Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in ChangeManager.last_changes() that exposes workspaces the viewer cannot view by skipping Workspace.can_view() checks site-wide. Anonymous visitors on instances with REQUIRE_LOGIN disabled and only public projects can query /changes/, /api/changes/, or RSS/CSV feeds to obtain hidden workspace names, UUIDs, actions, and timestamps.

t: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 Open Redirect via redirectUri on /pay/[id]
d: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to send users to arbitrary sites by supplying an unvalidated redirectUri parameter on the /pay/[id] payment link page. Attackers can distribute payment links with a malicious redirectUri that PayPageWidget opens via window.open after payment without noopener, enabling phishing and reverse tabnabbing of the payment page.

t: Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 Hard-coded Django SECRET_KEY in Default Settings
d: Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 contains a hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge signed data by using the publicly known Django SECRET_KEY in tcms/settings/common.py. Attackers can forge or tamper with signed cookie-based messages and django.core.signing payloads, weakening password-reset and session-authentication HMACs on deployments keeping the default.

t: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 Missing Authorization via fetchClientSecret Server Action
d: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

t: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 Missing Authorization in Cache Revalidation Server Actions
d: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in revalidatePathAction and revalidateCacheTagAction server actions in revalidate.ts. Unauthenticated attackers can use action identifiers exposed in the client bundle to send POST requests that purge cached pages and data, forcing repeated regeneration and degrading performance.

t: Unrolled Secure before 1.18.0 SSLRedirect Bypass via Absolute-Form Request-Target
d: Unrolled Secure before 1.18.0 contains an SSLRedirect bypass vulnerability in Secure.isSSL() that trusts the client-supplied r.URL.Scheme to determine HTTPS transport. Attackers can send plaintext HTTP requests with an absolute-form https:// request-target to skip the HTTPS redirect and have application responses served unencrypted.

t: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 Information Disclosure via Team Join Page
d: thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read non-public team metadata by requesting the team join page with any invite ID. Attackers who know a team slug can obtain the serialized Team object, exposing billing email, billing status, Stripe customer ID, verified domain and support identifiers.

t: Cetmix Tower through 17.0.3.0.0 and 18.0 before 18.0.4.0.1 Improper SSH Host Key Verification
d: Cetmix Tower through 17.0.3.0.0 and 18.0 before 18.0.4.0.1 contains an improper SSH host key verification vulnerability in SSHConnection.connect() that falls back to Paramiko's AutoAddPolicy when no host key is pinned. On-path attackers using ARP or DNS spoofing can present their own host key during Skip Host Key or Get from Host connections to capture stored SSH passwords and tamper with commands and files.

t: Kunai Mount Namespace Cache TOCTOU Allows Incorrect Event Resolution Against Host Files
d: Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in its mount namespace (mnt ns) caching logic. When resolving a security event that references a specific process PID and an expected mount namespace, the Switcher::new function read /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt to determine the target namespace and cached the result under the expected namespace key without verifying that the resolved namespace actually matched the expected one. An attacker with local access could exploit this by either (1) arranging for the referenced PID to be reused by a process in a different namespace (e.g., the host namespace) before Kunai resolves it, or (2) calling unshare or setns on the target process after the event is generated but before the namespace is resolved. In either case, the wrong namespace (potentially the host's own namespace) would be cached under the container's namespace key. The security impact is that subsequent container security events would be resolved against host filesystem paths rather than container paths. This undermines the integrity of the security monitoring data: container activity could be misattributed to the host, host activity could be misattributed to a container, and file-path-based detections or alerts would reference incorrect paths. An attacker could potentially use this to obscure malicious activity within a container by making it appear as benign host activity, or to generate misleading security alerts. The vulnerability requires local access to the system and a specific timing window between event generation and namespace resolution. No remote attack vector or user interaction is required.

t: Apache Shiro: PropertiesRealm reload does not remove deleted users or narrowed permissions
d: When PropertiesRealm reloads its properties file, removed users and narrowed permissions could remain in effect. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when PropertiesRealm`loads its properties from a file, which is reloaded periodically by default. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue. Alternatively, restart the application after removing users or narrowing permissions.

t: Apache Shiro: Empty stored credential matches an empty submitted password
d: `DefaultPasswordService` and `SimpleCredentialsMatcher` could treat an empty stored credential as a match for an empty submitted password. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when accounts with an empty stored credential exist. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue. Alternatively, avoid storing empty credentials, and reject empty passwords in the application.

t: Apache Shiro: Possible session fixation with RememberMe
d: Apache Shiro is vulnerable to session fixation when a user is authenticated via the "Remember me" functionality. In affected versions, when a subject is restored from a "Remember me" cookie, the existing session is not invalidated, nor is a new session created with a new ID. Additionally, session IDs were accepted from the request URL even when session ID URL rewriting was disabled. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when RememberMe functionality is enabled. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by invalidating the existing session and creating a new session with a new ID when a subject is restored from a "Remember me" cookie, and by ignoring session IDs in the URL when URL rewriting is disabled.

t: Apache Shiro: Authorization annotations not always enforced, depending on where they are placed
d: Authorization annotations, such as @RequiresRoles and @RequiresPermissions, are not always enforced in some class or interface hierarchies. Annotations declared on an interface were not enforced when using the shiro-guice, shiro-aspectj, shiro-cdi or shiro-jakarta-ee modules. In addition, annotations declared on a class or a superclass were not always enforced when using shiro-guice or shiro-aspectj, allowing an unauthorized caller to invoke methods that should be protected. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, with impact depending on module and where annotations are declared. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue. The annotation closest to the invoked method now takes precedence. Alternatively, declare authorization annotations directly on each protected implementing method.

t: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via truncated multipart part past the parts limit
d: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, when a request reaches the configured limit on the number of multipart parts, each further part is skipped without attaching an error listener to the skipped part stream. If the request body ends in the middle of such a skipped part, the vendored Dicer parser emits an error on that stream, and because nothing is listening Node.js raises an unhandled error event and the process exits. A single crafted unauthenticated request is therefore enough to crash the server. The bug is latent in the parser on its own and was first demonstrated through @fastify/multipart versions 10.1.2 through 10.1.4, which keep feeding the request body to the parser after a limit error, and it affects any consumer that sets a finite parts limit and parses request bodies that can be terminated early. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. There is no complete application level workaround because the crash happens inside the parser before application code runs, though consumers that set a finite parts limit should also attach an error listener to the parser stream.

t: Apache Shiro: Saved form replay may weaken cookie security and expose form data
d: When Apache Shiro is used with the Jakarta EE integration module, the automatic form saving feature weakens the security of a form that is resubmitted after login. Cookies set by the application during the resubmission could lose their security attributes, such as `Secure` and `SameSite`. In addition, the resubmitted form data and cookies could be sent to an untrusted host. This issue affects Apache Shiro from 2.0.0-alpha through 3.0.1, only when using `shiro-jakarta-ee` integration module with form saving enabled (the default). Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which no longer replays the form over the network, and avoids this class of issues entirely. Alternatively, you can set the `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-host` (String) and `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-port` (Integer) system properties to restrict the host and port that Shiro will connect to when resubmitting a form.

t: Apache Shiro: Principal tags in Jakarta Pages and Jakarta Faces do not escape output, allowing cross-site scripting
d: The shiro:principal tags in shiro-web (Jakarta Pages) and shiro-jakarta-ee (Jakarta Faces) did not escape their output, which could allow cross-site scripting when a principal value is not fully trusted. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when the principal tag is used. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which escapes the output. Alternatively, validate principal values on input.

t: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to multipart file/field type confusion via chunk-dependent header parsing
d: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 3.2.1 through 3.2.5, the parser can interpret the same multipart bytes differently depending on how they are split across socket reads: when the sequence that terminates a part's header block arrives split exactly at the configured header size limit, an off by one error drops the final header line, so a part declared as a binary file attachment is emitted as an ordinary text field instead of a file. A remote client controls both the multipart body and the header padding needed to reach the boundary and can influence segmentation, so an application that applies upload validation such as malware scanning or extension checks only to file events while trusting plain field values may process the payload through the wrong path. The parser level type confusion is fully reproducible, while the downstream validation bypass depends on the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which tracks how many terminator bytes were actually buffered when the limit is reached so a split terminator no longer corrupts the final header, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, apply the same validation to field values as to file uploads rather than treating file events as a trust boundary.

t: Apache Shiro: Incorrect default for case-insensitive path matching in ShiroFilterFactoryBean allows auth bypass for static files
d: The fix for CVE-2026-23903 https://shiro.apache.org/security-reports.html#cve_2026_23903 was incomplete for manually-created ShiroFilterFactoryBean, which still matched paths case-sensitively by default. This issue affects Apache Shiro version 3.0.1, only when ShiroFilterFactoryBean is created manually by the application and static files are served from a case-insensitive filesystem. Applications that let Shiro Spring (Boot) Starter create the bean are not affected. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue. Alternatively, call setCaseInsensitive(true) on the ShiroFilterFactoryBean.

t: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via URL-encoded field size-limit bypass
d: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart and url-encoded form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, the url-encoded parser stops accumulating a field only when the decoded length exactly equals the configured per-field size limit, and a malformed percent escape is passed through verbatim by the decoder, so the decoded length can jump from just below the limit to just above it and skip that equality check. The parser then keeps buffering the field in memory until the next delimiter or the end of the request, so a single unauthenticated url-encoded field or field name can grow to the size of the whole request body regardless of a much smaller configured per-field limit, with memory use bounded only by the independent whole-request body limit. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which clamps a field as soon as the decoded length reaches or exceeds the limit, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, set a conservative whole-request body limit so the per-field overshoot cannot exceed it.

t: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via a multipart part with unterminated headers
d: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, a multipart part whose header block is never terminated before the next boundary is counted by the vendored Dicer parser as an open part that never ends, so the parser emits neither a finish nor an error event and the request hangs. A single unauthenticated request of roughly one hundred bytes triggers the stall, and through @fastify/multipart the hung handler is not released when the client disconnects, so repeated requests leak handlers and whatever resources they hold, such as files, database connections and concurrency slots, until the process is restarted. The same parser is reached by the formData methods of undici versions 5.25.3 through 6.7.0. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, configure Fastify's handler timeout so hung handlers are eventually terminated and their resources released.

t: @fastify/multipart vulnerable to arbitrary file write via type confusion in saveRequestFiles()
d: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 7.4.0 through 10.1.8, when the plugin is registered with the attachFieldsToBody option, the saveRequestFiles helper treats any object in the parsed request body that carries truthy file and buffer properties as an uploaded file. An unauthenticated client can forge such an object through a plain JSON request or a JSON-typed multipart field, so attacker-chosen bytes are written to the temporary directory while upload hooks and the file count and size limits are skipped, and the saved entry keeps the attacker's filename verbatim instead of being reduced to its basename. Because that filename can contain parent directory segments, applications that use it as a write destination, as the project README example does, are exposed to an arbitrary relative-path file write from a single request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.9, and users should upgrade to 10.1.9 or later. As a workaround, call saveRequestFiles only after confirming the request is multipart, and reduce each returned filename to its basename or validate it against an allowlist before using it as a destination.

t: Sensitive information disclosure via API
d: The vulnerability enables any attacker with admin access to dump credentials of all accounts stored on the device, which can then be reused for lateral movement or further compromise. Since passwords are stored or processed in a recoverable format, this represents a critical failure in secure credential handling.

t: @fastify/multipart vulnerable to Denial of Service via temporary file leak after client disconnect
d: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 3.0.0 through 10.1.3, temporary files written by the saveRequestFiles helper are removed only by a response hook that runs when the response finishes or errors. When a client completes an upload and then disconnects before the handler writes the reply, for example while the handler scans, hashes or forwards the file, the response only emits a close event, the cleanup hook never runs, and the saved files are left on disk. An unauthenticated client can repeat this cheaply to exhaust disk space and deny service to applications that save uploaded files to disk. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.4, and users should upgrade to 10.1.4 or later. As a workaround, avoid saving request files for untrusted clients, or clean the saved files from a close handler on the raw response so removal also happens when the client disconnects.

t: @fastify/proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via ignored IPv6 zone identifier
d: @fastify/proxy-addr determines which network hops are trusted proxies and backs Fastify's trustProxy setting, so that forwarded headers can be believed. In versions 3.0.0 through 5.1.2, when trustProxy is configured with a zoned IPv6 link-local address, the trust comparison checks only the address bits and ignores the zone identifier, so a host on another link of a multi-homed server that carries the same link-local address is trusted as well. Such an attacker can spoof the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers, making the client IP, host and protocol reported by Fastify attacker-chosen values and defeating IP allowlists, rate limiting and audit logging. Exploitation requires a multi-homed server whose trustProxy is a zoned link-local address and an attacker directly on one of its other links; the default configuration and global, private or loopback trust entries are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/proxy-addr 5.1.3, and users should upgrade to 5.1.3 or later. As a workaround, avoid trusting a zoned link-local address on a multi-homed host and trust a global, private or loopback proxy address instead.

t: Information Exposure Through Error Message in visualTicket
d: visualTicket exposes sensitive information in error messages in the cinema report generator. An authenticated attacker with an admin privileges can supply an invalid date_from value causing the application to return a detailed error page that discloses the full SELECT statement (table and column names, JOIN, GROUP BY and ORDER BY clauses, bind parameter placeholders) and a PHP DateTime parsing exception. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Exposure of KSeF API Integration Secret in visualTicket
d: visualTicket displays secret token value in admin settings panel. The "KSeF - Token API" edit form renders a pre-filled field containing the actual KSeF API integration secret without any masking. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Information Exposure Through Error Message in visualTicket
d: visualTicket exposes sensitive information in error messages in the administrative report generator. Because application exception details and SQL queries are rendered in the HTTP response in the production environment, an authenticated administrator submitting an invalid date_from value in the report request receives a detailed error page disclosing the full SELECT statement, table and column names, JOINs, bind parameters, and a PHP DateTime exception. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Missing Authorization in visualTicket
d: visualTicket does not require authentication for the PDF invoice file serving functionality. Invoice PDF files reside in a web-accessible static path without a session check, while authorization is enforced only at the invoice registry page. A remote unauthenticated attacker who obtains the URL of an invoice PDF can download the document without authorization. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the selectedDate parameter in the order summary page. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Cross-Site Request Forgery in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) across multiple endpoints. State-changing operations are exposed via GET requests without any CSRF protection. A remote attacker can persuade an authenticated user (including administrator) into navigating to a prepared URL, causing the victim's browser to issue requests that carry the active session cookie and perform unintended actions. This issue was partially addressed in version 20260817: settings changes and bulk refunds require POST with a CSRF token, and the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which limits cross-site requests.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the JSONP callback parameter. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Information Exposure via JSONP in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through JSONP on session-bound cart service endpoints. Session-bound data (including the session id, cart id, item ids, ticket/event metadata, quantities and prices) is returned inside a script wrapper, and since the symfony session token can also be passed in the URL, a remote attacker who obtains the token can read the cart session token and cart data. This issue was mitigated in version 20260817: the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which prevents other websites from reading cart data of the victim’s session.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in logon functionality. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Session Fixation in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Session Fixation via the symfony session identifier passed in the URL. The application accepts the symfony session ID from the query string and set it as a session cookie in the HTTP response, allowing the browser's active session to be overwritten. This behaviour enables an attacker to fix a session ID for a victim and later hijack the authenticated session. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the "culture" and "sf_culture" parameters. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the error page in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Information Exposure Through Error Message in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through an error message in the order creation functionality. Because detailed data-layer exceptions are returned to the client instead of being logged server-side only, a remote unauthenticated attacker can submit a valid checkout request with an invalid payment_type value, causing the application to return a detailed SQL/ORM error that discloses the database name, table and column names, query structure, and foreign key constraint name. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Path Traversal in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the thumbnail generation mechanism. The file parameter is used directly when constructing the output filesystem path without restriction to the uploads directory, allowing a remote attacker to use ../ sequences to escape /uploads/user_temp_images/ and write the generated JPEG file to other writable locations, including the web root. This allows unauthorized creation of JPEG files outside the intended uploads directory, leading to file-space pollution and potential overwriting of predictable resources with matching names. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Insecure Direct Object Reference in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in the cart service. The server modifies or deletes a cart item based solely on the supplied "cart_id" without checking whether the object belongs to the current symfony session. Cart identifiers are created sequentially and allows prediction of valid values. An attacker holding an independent session can reference another user's "cart_id" and change its state, for example altering the quantity or deleting the item. This allows modification or deletion of items in another user's cart, alteration of the cart total, and disruption of the reservation/purchase process. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Remote Code Execution in Batflat CMS
d: Batflat CMS does not sanitize data passed to the /contact endpoint. A remote unauthenticated attacker can send a POST request with a crafted message, causing arbitrary PHP code execution with www-data user privileges. The project is no longer maintained and the issue has not been fixed.

t: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPER
d: A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could lead to an unauthenticated remote code execution.

In affected versions of Octopus Server, a user with permission to edit team scoped roles could escalate their privileges to deploy to projects and environments that they were not authorised to so.

t: Netskope Client and Endpoint DLP Local Privilege Escalation via Insecure OpenSSL Configuration
d: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Privilege Escalation via /kal-api/auth/user/edit
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify any account via the /kal-api/auth/user/edit endpoint. Attackers holding only read permission can set their admin flag and 'all' permission or reset an administrator's password to fully take over the instance.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Git Credential Disclosure via Documentation API
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated read-only users to retrieve Git deployment credentials via documentation API responses. Attackers can query GET /kal-api/docs/documentations or POST /kal-api/docs/documentation to obtain plaintext gitUser and gitPassword values and authenticate to external Git repositories.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Stored XSS via Unrestricted File Upload
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows read-only authenticated users to upload HTML or SVG files via the upload-file endpoint without type restrictions. Attackers can share links to files served unauthenticated through the file get route, executing JavaScript in the admin origin to steal administrator JWTs from localStorage.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Authentication Bypass via viewToken Cookie
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in RsPressMiddleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private documentation by supplying any non-empty viewToken cookie. Attackers can send requests with a forged viewToken cookie, which is never validated as a JWT, to read all pages and assets of RequireAuth documentation sites.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Unauthenticated File Upload via @tensei/media files/upload
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the @tensei/media plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload dangerous file types via the files/upload route. Attackers can set the multipart Content-Type to upload HTML or SVG files served from the application origin, causing stored cross-site scripting and storage consumption.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Unauthenticated Prototype Pollution via sort Parameter
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in parseSortFromStringToObject of @tensei/rest that allows unauthenticated attackers to set Object.prototype properties via the sort parameter. Attackers can send a sort value like __proto__.<name>:<value> to list, fetch-one, update or delete routes before authorization, altering application logic and causing denial of service.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Privilege Escalation via Self-Assigned Roles in @tensei/auth
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in @tensei/auth that allows unauthenticated or authenticated users to assign themselves arbitrary roles via the exposed User Roles field. Attackers can supply a roles array during registration, a POST to the users route, or a PATCH to their own record to gain administrator permissions.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Authentication Bypass via Hard-Coded JWT Secret in @tensei/auth
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in @tensei/auth that falls back to the hard-coded JWT signing key 'auth-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset. Unauthenticated attackers can sign tokens with arbitrary user ids accepted by populateContextFromToken to impersonate any user, including administrators.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Open Redirect via @tensei/social-auth OAuth Callback
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the @tensei/social-auth SocialAuthCallbackController that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying an unvalidated clientCallback query parameter. Attackers can craft links to the /:provider/callback route that send victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing and leak the issued temporary access token appended after login.

t: A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability
d: A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability in Pebble’s installers could allow a local attacker with low privilege access to place a malicious Dynamic Link Library (DLL) where a privileged executable file will load it.

t: A kernel pool buffer overflow vulnerability
d: A kernel pool buffer overflow vulnerability in the ct0531fl.sys file of the Creative WDM Audio Driver (64-bit), Sound Blaster Audigy 4 and Sound Blaster Audigy 5/Rx could allow a local attacker with low privilege access to cause a denial of service.

t: Mattermost Desktop App local network access filter bypass via secondary windows
d: Mattermost Desktop App versions <=6.3 6.0.3 6.3.2.0 fail to monitor secondary browser windows in the local network access filter which allows an attacker-controlled server to access private network resources via opening pop-out or widget windows. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00778

t: A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability
d: A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability in the Audigy Rx driver’s Emupia2k.sys file could allow a local attacker with low privilege access to gain higher privileges, such as administrator rights.

t: Insecure deserializaiton in the httpx Ruby gem via unsafe Oj object-mode
d: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

t: Denial of service in Mattermost Desktop via crafted file download
d: Mattermost Desktop App versions <=6.3 6.0.3 6.3.2.0 fail to handle filesystem errors that can occur when finalizing certain file downloads, which allows a malicious or compromised server to cause a denial of service by crashing the entire desktop application via a specially crafted download Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00779

t: udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block() When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash like: Oops: general protection fault KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503) Call Trace: vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419) do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583) __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602) This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being treated as a folio pointer with obvious results. Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either 0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.

t: nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners() client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140 fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners() nfsd4_exchange_id nfsd4_proc_compound nfsd_dispatch svc_process Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner list.

t: ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc() When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed, Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd. unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset); int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset; if (!dacl_offset || (dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size)) goto out; Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check") fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out, because it is only valid for 32-bit builds. t: usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512. The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c ("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means. But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to 1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this. As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.

t: ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire: ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then overwrites it with the size of the "in" set. t: ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps + num_prior_parent_snaps). t: virtio_net: atomically disable rx mode work
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_net: atomically disable rx mode work virtio-net uses a boolean to gate rx_mode_work during device teardown.
